sections.what_happened: An explosion at the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) headquarters in Baghdad killed one member and wounded four others, per a security and a medical source (Reuters). The PMF said a stockpile of obsolete ammunition exploded, injuring five people and causing a fire since brought under control. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi ordered an investigation into the blast. Al Arabiya's correspondent first reported an explosion heard near PMU HQ (TimesNow liveblog).
sections.what_verified: Reuters, Arab News, AA, azeritimes, TOI, bdnews24, devdiscourse all carry the same incident; Al Arabiya via TimesNow liveblog; Iraqi PM investigation order via official statement
sections.what_disputed: Cause ('obsolete ammunition') is the PMF's own account — no independent confirmation; the PMF statement reported no fatalities while security/medical sources confirmed one death and four injuries; no evidence of external attack, but investigation is open and the cause is not yet adjudicated
sections.why_matters: Baghdad is where the 'accidents' always matter: one dead at the PMF's own headquarters while Washington says Tehran can't pay its proxies. Keep the cause conditional on screen ('PMF says obsolete ammunition; Iraqi PM investigating'); the open loop is the investigation, not the explosion.
sections.context: Background: Iraq — NEW (missed by all prior scans): explosion at PMF headquarters in Baghdad kills 1, wounds 4; group blames obsolete ammunition; Iraqi PM orders investigation

totw_analysis: Our read: Baghdad is where the 'accidents' always matter: one dead at the PMF's own headquarters while Washington says Tehran can't pay its proxies. Keep the cause conditional on screen ('PMF says obsolete ammunition; Iraqi PM investigating'); the open loop is the investigation, not the explosion. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Accident in an old ammo dump — or the first strike of a new front against Iran's Iraqi allies?
